title: Generate complete help from dynamically discovered yargs command modules
objective: Refactor the sdlc CLI so the main entry point recursively discovers yargs command modules, registers every resolved command for dispatch and help, and keeps command-specific implementation functions encapsulated in their command files.

branch.name: WI-0033-dynamic-command-help
branch.rationale: The command-module refactor must be planned on main and processed on a dedicated context branch before primary-branch release.

request.text: Determine why work-item validate exists but is missing from sdlc -h, then prepare a new work item that refactors help and dispatch around dynamically discovered yargs command files. Each resolved command must automatically contribute help, command-specific implementation functions must remain inside command files, implementation and review work must be split into bounded batches, and final validation and release tasks must be included.

scope.name: command-module-contract
scope.description: Define and apply a typed yargs-compatible command factory contract for every current sdlc command.
scope.reason: A shared descriptor is required for one registry to drive both dispatch and help.

scope.name: dynamic-command-discovery
scope.description: Recursively enumerate, sort, dynamically import, validate, and register command files from source and compiled command directories.
scope.reason: The current manually maintained help table omits implemented commands such as work-item validate and task validate.

scope.name: complete-command-migration
scope.description: Migrate work-item, repository, task, reference, and stat command paths into command files while preserving current interfaces and output contracts.
scope.reason: All resolved commands must automatically appear in help and remain dispatchable.

scope.name: encapsulated-command-functions
scope.description: Keep command-specific option handling, orchestration, output shaping, and handlers in the corresponding command file; keep main.ts as composition only.
scope.reason: Command files must own their behavior so adding a command does not require editing a central dispatch/help table.

scope.name: release-evidence
scope.description: Validate the complete command/help surface and perform the next primary-branch revision release after all implementation and review gates pass.
scope.reason: The requested change modifies the public CLI interface and requires a traceable release boundary.

nonGoals.name: command-semantics-change
nonGoals.description: Do not change the domain behavior, JSON response schemas, option meanings, reference semantics, or task identifier syntax of existing commands.
nonGoals.reason: This work item addresses command resolution, help generation, and encapsulation rather than command business logic.

nonGoals.name: untrusted-plugin-loading
nonGoals.description: Do not introduce network command discovery, arbitrary plugin execution, shell command execution, or an authorization bypass through filesystem enumeration.
nonGoals.reason: Only repository-owned command modules under the declared command roots are in scope.

nonGoals.name: production-deployment
nonGoals.description: Do not claim production deployment, remote publication, or server-side enforcement from local CLI tests and release evidence.
nonGoals.reason: The evidence boundary is the local package, linked executable, repository tests, and primary-branch tag.

items.name: command-module-contract
items.description: Every command file must export a typed yargs-compatible command factory with command, describe, builder, and handler members, and command-specific implementation functions must remain in that file.
items.reason: A stable contract enables dynamic registration while preserving command encapsulation.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The design document defines the command factory interface, required yargs members, source/compiled module paths, and the rule that command-specific functions are implemented inside each command file.
All twelve current command paths are represented by command files conforming to the interface, and main.ts contains only root composition, discovery, registration, parsing, and exit-code mapping.

items.name: dynamic-command-discovery
items.description: The main CLI dynamically enumerates repository-owned command files, imports them deterministically, rejects invalid or duplicate descriptors, and registers all valid commands before help or dispatch.
items.reason: Root help must automatically include every command that the CLI can resolve and execute.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Recursive source and compiled command-folder enumeration is deterministic, suffix-aware, relative to the executing module, and fails closed on module-load or descriptor errors.
Duplicate command paths and malformed command modules are rejected before yargs exposes help or dispatch.

items.name: complete-command-help
items.description: Root and command-specific help must be generated by yargs from the same registered command descriptors used for dispatch.
items.reason: The current hard-coded printHelp table omits work-item validate and task validate even though their handlers exist.

acceptanceCriteria.description: sdlc -h and sdlc --help list work-item validate, task validate, and every other resolved command without a second manually maintained command inventory.
Every current command-specific --help path exits successfully and documents its yargs options, including work-item validate --help and task validate --help.

items.name: behavior-preservation
items.description: The migration preserves existing command paths, option forms, output schemas, errors, repository-root resolution, read/write boundaries, and global help/version aliases.
items.reason: The refactor must correct help completeness without silently changing established CLI behavior.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The complete test suite, typecheck, build, command-help matrix, representative dispatch smoke tests, and WI-0033 validation pass.
The installed user-local sdlc executable is verified after linking/build delivery and reports the released package version.

items.name: review-and-release-traceability
items.description: Bounded implementation/review pairs, aggregate validation, the root design document, and a primary-branch revision release remain traceable in the WI-0033 task graph.
items.reason: The command refactor spans multiple command families and needs small review contexts plus a final release gate.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every implementation and review task references command-module-pattern.md; every review checks adherence and command-file encapsulation; final validation and release reference the same design.
The complete WI-0033 object tree validates with no unresolved references before merge or release.

versionSuggestion.rationale: Refactors the public CLI command registration and help generation while preserving existing command semantics and output contracts.
versionSuggestion.disclaimer: This is an inferred recommendation; increase the impact if final changes add breaking command behavior or broader compatibility effects.
